transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

That musty smell is usually caused by trapped moisture and lint building up inside the machine rather than a broken part. The most common culprits are a blocked pump filter or a dirty condenser, which stop air from circulating properly during the cycle. To fix this safely, please switch off and unplug the washer-dryer first so it is safe to work on. Then place some towels and a shallow tray under the bottom-left corner of the machine before slowly unscrewing the pump filter to check for fluff or debris blocking the airflow.
ok unplugged it and had a look at the filter, theres loads of smelly sludge and fluff in there, proper grim. is that what's causing it?

Yes, that sludge and fluff are almost certainly causing the musty smell by trapping moisture and preventing proper airflow during the cycle. It is important to clean the filter thoroughly and let it dry before putting it back in to stop the odour from returning quickly. If you have already cleaned the filter but the clothes still smell damp after a wash, there may be another blockage or part issue specific to your model. Please check for the model number on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door so I can give you more precise advice.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
the model number on the sticker says WD80T554DBW. ive not cleaned the filter out yet, should i just rinse it and pop it back?

[Heading: Likely cause: lint filter]
Rinsing it is the right first step to remove the bulk of the sludge and fluff you found. However, for a WD80T554DBW washer-dryer, simply rinsing the filter may not be enough because these models often have a condenser unit that also traps lint and causes damp smells if it is blocked. I cannot find a confirmed match for this specific model in my current knowledge base to tell you exactly where that condenser is located or how to access it safely. To avoid damaging your machine, I would suggest checking the Samsung website for official cleaning instructions for your model or contacting their spares department for guidance on accessing the internal lint trap.
